body:
## Summary
The diff itself (nav entry + doc update) is correct in isolation, but merging this PR as-is right now will break site navigation and ship inaccurate docs, because the two dependencies it needs (`/changelog` page and `lib/changelog.ts`) are not actually present on `main` or on this branch.

## Architecture & Design

- **[BLOCKING] Merging now introduces a live 404 on every page.** `components/portal-nav.tsx` renders `navGroups.flatMap(...)` in the global top nav on every route, and `pathname.startsWith(item.href)` is evaluated for every link, including the new one. I checked out this branch and ran `npm run build`; the route manifest confirms there is no `/changelog` route anywhere in the app (`app/changelog/page.tsx` does not exist on this branch or on `main` — it only exists on the unmerged `feature/changelog-page` branch). Any visitor on any page will see a "Changelog" link in the header that 404s when clicked. This isn't hypothetical — it's directly demonstrated by the build output and the file tree.
- **[BLOCKING] Docs now describe a module that doesn't exist in the codebase.** `docs/architecture.md` is updated to list `lib/changelog.ts` as a shipped module, but `lib/changelog.ts` does not exist on this branch (only on the separate unmerged `feature/changelog-data-feed` branch). Merging this leaves `main` with documentation that misrepresents the actual module layout.
- **PM/dependency tracking mismatch confirms this is a real gap, not a false alarm.** The linked Trello card's own "Dependencies" checklist has both dependency items unchecked (`/changelog` page, `lib/changelog.ts` data feed), yet a card comment claims dependencies are "already in DONE." The PR author acknowledged this discrepancy in the PR description and filed a friction report, but the practical effect is unchanged: this PR should not be merged to `main` ahead of (or independently of) `feature/changelog-page` and `feature/changelog-data-feed`. Recommend holding this PR (or marking it draft) until those two land, or merging all three together/in the correct order.

## Code Issues
None — the nav entry (`{ href: "/changelog", label: "Changelog" }`) is placed correctly per the acceptance criteria, and the diagram edit follows the existing doc convention. Local verification of the stated test plan (`npm run test`, `npm run build`, `npx eslint lib/garage-content.ts --max-warnings 0`) all reproduce successfully on this branch.

## Questions
- Is there a reason this PR was opened/landed ahead of its two dependencies rather than after them, given the card's own dependency checklist shows both as incomplete?

## Summary
The PR branch currently contains **zero net changes relative to `main`** — the second commit (`01e242c`) fully reverts everything the first commit (`344fcd8`) added. `git diff origin/main...pr/30` is empty, and neither `lib/garage-content.ts` nor `docs/architecture.md` contain any "changelog" reference on this branch. Yet the PR title, description, and the linked card's acceptance-criteria checklist still claim the nav link and doc updates were added and verified. Requesting changes because the PR as it stands is misleading and doesn't advance the work item.

## Architecture & Design
- **[BLOCKING] PR is now a no-op but is titled/described as shipping a feature.** Commit `344fcd8` added the `/changelog` nav entry and the `lib/changelog.ts` doc reference; commit `01e242c` reverted both in full (confirmed via `git show <commit> --stat` for each, and via an empty `git diff origin/main...pr/30`). The PR title (`feat(nav): add Changelog link to Explore nav group and docs`), description, and test-plan checkboxes still describe the original (now-reverted) change as if it's what will land. Merging this PR in its current state does nothing toward the "As a visitor, I want the Changelog linked in nav and docs" goal — it's an empty diff dressed up as a feature PR.
- **Linked Trello card's Acceptance Criteria are checked off but no longer true.** The checklist item "`lib/garage-content.ts` navGroups Explore group includes `{ href: "/changelog", label: "Changelog" }` directly after the Backlog entry" is marked done, but that entry was removed by the revert commit. Same for the two `docs/architecture.md` checklist items. These should be unchecked (or the PR closed/reopened once dependencies land) rather than left showing false completion.
- The underlying reasoning for the revert itself is correct and was caught well by the prior automated review (dependency ordering — `/changelog` page and `lib/changelog.ts` don't exist on `main` yet). That part of the process worked. The problem is the PR was left in this halfway state (opened, "fixed" back to a no-op) rather than being closed/converted to draft, or resubmitted once `feature/changelog-page` and `feature/changelog-data-feed` are actually merged.

## Recommendation
Either:
1. Close this PR (or convert to draft) until `feature/changelog-page` and `feature/changelog-data-feed` land on `main`, then reopen with the actual nav link + doc changes, or
2. If it must stay open, update the title/description to reflect that it currently contains no functional changes and is blocked on dependencies, and uncheck the now-false acceptance criteria on the linked card.

No inline comments are attached since the diff between `main` and this branch is empty — there are no changed lines to annotate.

## Summary
The diff itself is a safe, well-justified no-op (an explanatory code comment), but the PR's title and description are stale and no longer describe what the diff actually does — this needs to be corrected before merge.

## Architecture & Design

- **[SHOULD_FIX] PR title/description are inaccurate relative to the current diff.** After two prior review rounds, commit `344fcd8` (which added the real `/changelog` nav link + `docs/architecture.md` update) was fully reverted by `01e242c`, and the only change now on this branch relative to `main` is commit `31dc4f4`, which adds a 6-line explanatory comment to `lib/garage-content.ts` noting the link is deferred. I confirmed via `git diff origin/main...HEAD` that `docs/architecture.md` has zero changes and `lib/garage-content.ts` has no `/changelog` entry — I also confirmed neither `app/changelog/page.tsx` nor `lib/changelog.ts` exist anywhere in this branch or `main`, so deferring is the right call. However, the PR title (`feat(nav): add Changelog link to Explore nav group and docs`) and the "## Summary" bullets in the description still claim the nav link was added and the docs were updated — neither is true anymore. A reviewer or future maintainer scanning merged PR history would be misled about what actually shipped. Please update the title/description to reflect that this PR now only adds a deferred-work comment (e.g. `docs(nav): note why Changelog link is deferred`), or hold/close the PR until `feature/changelog-page` and `feature/changelog-data-feed` land, per the prior reviewer's own recommendation.
- The work item's acceptance criteria for the actual nav link and doc updates remain unaddressed (correctly left unchecked on the card), since those depend on the two unmerged branches. That's expected given the current no-op state, but it means this PR alone does not advance the linked story's goal ("visitor can discover Changelog in nav") — worth being explicit about in the PR body so it isn't mistaken for the completed story.

## Code Issues
None in the actual line-level change — the added comment is accurate, references the correct tracking card, and doesn't touch runtime behavior. `app/changelog` and `lib/changelog.ts` are confirmed absent from this branch, so deferring the link is correct and avoids the dead-link/stale-docs issues flagged in earlier review rounds.

## Questions
- Given the diff is now functionally empty relative to `main` (aside from the comment), should this PR be converted to draft / held until the two dependency branches merge, rather than staying open as a "feat" PR that ships no feature?

## Summary
The diff has settled into a safe, comment-only no-op: two prior review rounds correctly caught that the actual nav link (`{ href: "/changelog", label: "Changelog" }`) and the `docs/architecture.md` update would ship a dead nav item (no `app/changelog/page.tsx` on `main`) and a doc reference to a non-existent module (`lib/changelog.ts`). Both were reverted (`01e242c`), and the only change remaining relative to `main` is a 6-line explanatory comment in `lib/garage-content.ts` documenting the deferral, plus a follow-up note pointing at the stale PR metadata. I verified independently:
- `git diff`-equivalent via `get-pr-diff --path docs/architecture.md` → no changes (file untouched).
- `get-pr-diff --path lib/garage-content.ts` → matches the pre-fetched diff exactly: comment-only addition, no `links` array mutation.
- CI is now green (lint/typecheck/test/build all passing).

This is technically correct and low-risk to merge as-is.

## Architecture & Design
- **[SHOULD_FIX] PR title/description no longer match the diff.** The title (`feat(nav): add Changelog link to Explore nav group and docs`) and the "## Summary"/"## Test plan" sections of the description still describe the original nav-link + docs change that was reverted two commits ago. If this is squash-merged, the commit message landing on `main` will misrepresent what actually shipped (a deferred-work comment, not a feature). This has already been raised in two prior review rounds and acknowledged by the author, who confirmed via testing that `cascade-tools scm create-pr` has no PR-metadata-edit path and filed a friction report on the gap. Since the author has exhausted the available tooling to fix this themselves (and has left an explicit in-code pointer for a human maintainer to retitle/close the PR), I'm not blocking merge on it — but a maintainer should manually correct the title/description before merging, e.g. to `docs(nav): note why Changelog link is deferred`, per the author's own suggested replacement text.
- The underlying dependency-ordering call (deferring the nav link until `feature/changelog-page` and `feature/changelog-data-feed` land) is correct and well-documented in the new comment, including a pointer to the tracking card and exact re-add instructions.

## Code Issues
None. The comment addition is accurate, doesn't affect runtime behavior, and I confirmed `app/changelog/page.tsx` and `lib/changelog.ts` are genuinely absent from `main`/this branch, so no dead link or doc drift is shipped by this PR.

## Recommendation
Approving on the merits of the actual code change (safe, correct, tested, zero functional risk). Flagging for a maintainer, outside this automated review loop, to fix the PR title/description before merge since no available tool can do that programmatically.
